name: Glanzmann Thrombasthenia

criteria.description: Absent or severely reduced platelet aggregation in response to ADP, collagen, and epinephrine
Normal platelet count and morphology on peripheral blood smear
Identification of pathogenic mutations in ITGA2B or ITGB3 genes
History of mucocutaneous bleeding such as epistaxis, gingival bleeding, or menorrhagia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of absent platelet aggregation with normal platelet count and morphology, plus clinical bleeding history
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing supports diagnosis but is not mandatory if functional platelet studies are conclusive.

pathognomonic.notes: Includes spontaneous bruising and prolonged bleeding from minor injuries
searchTerms: severe bleeding from skin and mucous membranes
heavy bleeding in mouth and skin

pathognomonic.symptomName: Absent platelet aggregation to multiple agonists
searchTerms: platelet function defect with no aggregation

pathognomonic.symptomName: Normal platelet count with defective clot retraction
searchTerms: normal platelet count but poor clot shrinking
blood clot retraction problem despite normal platelets
defective clot tightening with normal platelets

common.symptomName: Prolonged bleeding after surgery or dental extraction

occasional.notes: Less common than in coagulation factor deficiencies

searchTerms: low red blood cells from bleeding
anemia due to chronic blood loss

laboratory: Absent platelet aggregation with ADP, collagen, and epinephrine
imaging: Imaging may be required to evaluate bleeding complications such as intracranial hemorrhage
genetic: Mutations in ITGA2B gene encoding integrin alpha-IIb
Mutations in ITGB3 gene encoding integrin beta-3
other: Flow cytometry showing decreased or absent GPIIb/IIIa complex on platelet surface

distinguishingFeatures: Normal platelet aggregation to ADP and collagen but defective secondary aggregation

redFlags: Prolonged bleeding after minor trauma or surgery
references: Nurden AT. Glanzmann thrombasthenia. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2006;1:10.
George JN, Caen JP, Nurden AT. Glanzmann thrombasthenia: the spectrum of clinical disease. Blood. 1990;75(7):1383-95.
Seligsohn U. Glanzmann thrombasthenia: a review. Semin Thromb Hemost. 1993;19(4):353-60.
